title: Four optical effects matched to their phenomena by measurement: the aurora's line spectrum, polarized skylight, the rainbow and diffraction fringes
summary: Four stations, four measurements: the aurora shows atomic emission lines (5), skylight is polarized by molecular scattering (4), a raindrop disperses light with a partial internal reflection (1), and a slit gives dark fringes in one colour (3) - P5, Q4, R1, S3, option A.
subject: Physics
topic: Optical effects in nature and the phenomenon essential to each - emission, scattering, dispersion with reflection, diffraction
subtopics: Atomic emission: lambda = hc/dE gives discrete spectral lines (aurora: O 557.7 and 630.0 nm, N2+ 427.8 nm)
Scattering of light by molecules: the blue sky and the partial polarization of skylight, P = sin^2 theta/(1 + cos^2 theta)
The rainbow: dispersion n(lambda) and one internal reflection in a raindrop; minimum deviation
Single-slit diffraction: dark fringes at a sin theta = m lambda
Total internal reflection and the critical angle
concepts: The aurora is light emitted by oxygen and nitrogen excited by charged particles from the Sun: a line spectrum, not scattered sunlight
Light scattered by air molecules is partially polarized, fully (ideally) at 90 deg from the Sun; total internal reflection reflects both polarizations fully and cannot polarize
A rainbow needs dispersion and one internal reflection; inside the drop the ray meets the back at about 40 deg, below the critical angle 48.7 deg, so the reflection is partial, not total
Dark and bright fringes in light of one colour behind an opening are diffraction
P5 Q4 R1 S3: option A
answerValue: P->5, Q->4, R->1, S->3 (option A; key A)

methods: MathonGo solution (their Q30 = Physics Q.14) read first as the conceptual reference for the intended approach (one mechanism per effect); the answer then derived independently
P: aurora wavelengths from atomic energy levels (lambda = hc/dE) are discrete lines; Rayleigh-scattered sunlight (Planck x lambda^-4) is a smooth continuum peaking in the violet
Q: dipole scattering of unpolarized light summed numerically and in sympy gives P = sin^2/(1 + cos^2); Fresnel's equations show total internal reflection reflects s and p fully (no polarization)

R: a ray traced through a drop by coordinates and by Descartes' condition: rainbow at 42.4 (red) and 40.6 deg (violet); the internal angle 40.4 deg is below the critical angle 48.7 deg (Fresnel R about 11 %): partial, not total
S: a single slit summed as Huygens phasors is dark at a sin theta = m lambda for one colour; matches (sin b/b)^2
Every option audited: B, C and D each fail on at least one row
